agree.reason: The calm tone and the 74-of-112 figure push back on her view that this is a few loud people, but the letter leaves out the dialysis appointments, the stair chair and the rent credit. It also offers no commitments from the association, so its asks are vague enough that she could answer them with a status update and still feel the outages were handled well.

honest.reason: Most claims stay within the facts and are hedged ('may be unable'), but 'Five months later' assumes a timeline the brief doesn't give, and details like carrying children and visiting family are added colour, not supplied facts.

works_the_facts.reason: It works out the two-thirds share and contrasts the six-to-eight-week promise with months of waiting, but it never turns 41 days into a rate (more than one day in nine so far this year) or projects what happens if the part keeps slipping.

right_comparison.reason: It shows the status quo fairly as a part that is 'always six to eight weeks away' and separates passing inspection from reliability, but it doesn't show any trend in outages or the stakes of carrying on as now.

qualification.reason: The safety hedge is well drawn, but the one deadline is a '[date]' placeholder, and no ask names a checkable date or says what the association will do if it is missed (for example, the Channel 7 visit).

objections.reason: It meets the passing inspection and the infeasibility of a second elevator head-on without overclaiming, and the 74 signatures answer the 'loud few' view. It doesn't answer the claim that management has handled things well by offering the association's own help, such as the stairs-assistance list or evening meetings.

fit.reason: It is about the right length for an open letter, but it uses bracketed placeholders for the building, company, manager, secretary and dates, even though the writer was given those names, so it isn't ready to post in the lobby or send to the TV station.
